correctness.rationale: Putting h=t+1, rewrite the exponential generating function as e^(-z)/(1-h+h e^(-z)). Expanding in h/(1-h) gives the stated convergent p-adic moments; the coefficient at base b is a unit times h^(b-1). For an even shift the b=1 term cancels and b=2 has valuation s+ell. If ell=0 every other unit term has valuation at least 2s. If ell>0, then p-1 divides q and primitive-root lifting gives ell=1+v_p(q/(p-1)); Fermat and lifting give this as a lower bound on v_p(b^q-1) for every unit b. The other unit terms have valuation at least 2s+ell; the nonunit terms have valuation at least n. Thus at the stated threshold the leading term survives without cancellation. Reduction mod p^s leaves (-1)^n, making odd shifts units (p odd) and giving period two for a<=s. Above s, the exact even-shift formula and order of 2 modulo p^(a-s) give the minimal eventual period and stated onset. The supplied tests were inspected, not run; the proof and the independent coefficientwise/derivative argument establish the infinite claim.

broader_coverage.reasoning: For ell>0 the primitive-root hypothesis makes q a multiple of lambda(p^ell), and the indexed theorem gives the needed uniform coefficientwise divisibility for n>=ell. It does not state this parameter-sensitive exact valuation explicitly, but supplies it by the root and derivative argument below. The integral-substitution theorem gives related upper-period background, not a sharp scalar equality statement.

evidence: For even q, write P(X)=G_(n+q)(X)-G_n(X). The generating function at X=-1 is exp(-z), so P(-1)=0. Its X derivative there is exp(-z)-exp(-2z), giving P'(-1)=-(-2)^n(2^q-1).
Coefficientwise periodicity by lambda(p^ell) gives P in p^ell Z[X] for n>=ell when ell>0; when ell=0 the assertion is immediate from integrality.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Divide P by p^ell(X+1) in Z[X] to obtain K. Then K(-1)=P'(-1)/p^ell is a p-adic unit and K(t) has that same nonzero residue. This is the exact valuation s+ell, with onset n>=ell, stronger than required. The odd shift and low-modulus period follow from G_n(t) congruent to (-1)^n mod p^s; above s the condition is exactly 2^q=1 mod p^(a-s), whose least order is the asserted even period. Thus all clauses follow, not merely an upper period.

originality.rationale: The complete colored law is a short consequence of the distinct indexed coefficientwise periodicity theorem 6f2e97b87162 and the first derivative at -1. It is not just a specialization of the coefficientwise *least* period: the coefficientwise divisibility supplies the crucial factor, and the first derivative proves exactness at every allowed weight. This derives the same result at the stated onset and in fact for n>=ell. The two records are distinct; no priority inference is made from their shared catalogue date or from the unnamed archived record discussed in the related-work section.
residual_risks: The catalogue dates and unnamed scalar reference do not establish which record came first, and the Diagana–Maïga full text was unavailable. Neither uncertainty is the basis of the decision: the separately inspected coefficientwise theorem and the explicit implication are decisive.
